summary: Rabbi Soffer examines the halakhic status of using a towel taken from a hotel and left at a mikveh. He explores the concepts of Yeush and the prohibition against benefiting from a stolen object, using the Gemara's discussions on stolen wood and fallen figs as legal analogies. The class considers whether the hotel's general awareness of missing towels constitutes despair of ownership and how this impacts the obligation to return the object.
questions: Can I use a towel I find at a mikveh if I know it was taken from a hotel?
Does a hotel's general expectation that towels will go missing constitute Yeush?
Am I permitted to benefit from a stolen object if I do not intend to keep it?
Does the obligation to return a stolen object change if the thief has abandoned it?
Can a person acquire ownership of an object that was stolen by someone else?
